# developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Reference — Client Reference

> 6 page(s) of developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Reference under Client Reference. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Client Reference

- [Best Practices and Troubleshooting](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/best-practices/): It is best practice to place your `<script>` tag as close to the bottom of your HTML document as possible.
- [Browser Support](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/browser-support/): The Braintree JavaScript v2 SDK provides support for numerous browsers and devices. There are, however, caveats with certain integrations and browser combinations.
- [Configuration for braintree.setup](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/configuration/): Braintree.js integrations are created with `braintree.setup`.
- [Credit Cards](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/credit-cards/): Important For a merchant to be eligible for the easiest level of PCI compliance (SAQ A), payment fields can't be hosted on your checkout page.
- [Hosted Fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/hosted-fields/): You can subscribe to events using the `onFieldEvent` callback. This allows you to hook into `focus`, `blur`, and `fieldStateChange`.
- [PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/client-reference/javascript/v2/paypal/): The PayPal functionality of Braintree.js accepts a few different options. The below options can be used for all PayPal integration types (Vault, Checkout with PayPal).
